item.title: Designing a Coding Agent Without a KV Cache
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. A design note from September 2026 gathers six coding-agent complaints under one sentence. Suppose a language model had no KV cache. What would these agents look like then. The answer contains no stronger model. It contains one thing, someone deciding what goes in front of the model on every turn.

item.title: Why Go Is the Default Language of the Agent Era
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. In one line: once AI drives the cost of writing code to near zero, a language’s value moves from how it reads to how it is reviewed — and every trade-off Go made in its first fifteen years sits on the review side. The two source posts landed in the same month, from different authors, different starting points, and the same conclusion.

item.title: Super-agent: DeepSeek Takes Sessions Away From the User
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. In one line: the interesting claim in DeepSeek Harness’s architecture note is not its five modules — modules change with deployment. It is one sentence: sessions should be an implementation detail of the system, not a mental burden on its user. Everything below is that sentence, taken seriously. Published 2026-10-31, the note opens by telling you what it is not: an architecture discussion, not a description of shipping features.
